findings.text: s34 asserts the successor edge the apply wrote is inside the manifest digest ("That digest folds in each participant's closure, and the edge the apply wrote is part of the closure. So a supersede that writes an edge moves its own digest"), but in `imas_codex/standard_names/signed_manifest.py` the collateral snapshot's relationship set is `_RELATIONSHIP_TYPES = frozenset({"PRODUCED_NAME", "HAS_PARENT"})` (:59, applied at :2319), which excludes `HAS_SUCCESSOR`, and a node participant's snapshot returns `properties(node)` plus a property fingerprint only (:2253-2256), so a MERGE'd `HAS_SUCCESSOR` edge with no node-property write cannot move the digest; the supersede mutation does set node properties on the predecessor (`superseded_from_stage` coalesce, `source_paths`, `claimed_at`, `claim_token`, :4826-4832), so if the digest moved the cause is a participant-property change, not the edge — and the claimed discriminator "§31's rows wrote no edge, so their digest held" would then be wrong, since §31's rows ran the same `supersede` mutation.
